Chapter 12: Living with Purpose and Intention
You know, purpose is one of those words we hear all the time. But if you're like most people, it can feel a little out of reach. What does it actually mean to live with purpose? Is it about chasing big, flashy accomplishments? Or is it something quieter—something you feel deep down, even in the small moments?
I remember talking to a friend who was going through a major career shift. She was wrestling with those really big questions: Why am I here? What matters most to me? At first, the answers seemed impossible to find. But as she started tuning in to what made her feel alive—things like helping others, creating something beautiful, or just learning something new—she realized purpose isn’t about arriving at some final destination. It’s more about how you show up each day.
Here’s something to pay attention to—most of us don’t realize just how much intention shapes our experiences. When you line up your actions with your values, even the little things—like making coffee for a loved one or finishing a project at work—start to feel meaningful. But if you’re running on autopilot, it’s easy to drift and wonder where the meaning went.
I once heard a story about a teacher, getting ready to retire after many years in the classroom. He thought back on his career and realized his greatest joy didn’t come from awards or recognition, but from those quiet moments when he made a difference in someone’s life. Those small moments, over time, added up to a life filled with real purpose.
Living with purpose doesn’t mean you have to have a five-year plan, or a crystal-clear vision of the future. It’s really about noticing what matters to you, and then making choices—big and small—that reflect those values.
So often, people wait for some lightning bolt of clarity before they take action. But here’s the truth—purpose isn’t something you stumble upon by accident. It’s something you discover by doing.
Think about a parent juggling work and family. For them, meaning shows up in the daily routines—packing lunches, reading bedtime stories, going to school events. These everyday acts, though they might seem ordinary, become expressions of love and intention.
When you really look at it, purpose isn’t something you need to find. It’s something you create, moment by moment. Most of us don’t realize just how much power we have to shape our own lives—one choice at a time.
